_doc: Period layers the book needs (docs/PERIOD_LAYERS.md). Planning agents extend layers and snapshots; tracing agents fulfil one layer each with data/library/geo/<id>.geojson. npm run maps -- status shows progress.

snapshots.title: Before the war for the continent
After the Treaty of Paris and the Proclamation

layers.name: New France
sources: Treaty of Utrecht 1713 (Acadia, Newfoundland and Hudson Bay to Britain)
Bellin, "Carte de la Louisiane et des pays voisins" (1755)
Mitchell Map (1755) for the contested Ohio Country
layers.notes: Canada, the pays d'en haut around the Great Lakes, the Illinois Country and Louisiana on both banks of the Mississippi. The Ohio Country was claimed by both crowns: precision "contested".

layers.name: British mainland colonies
sources: Charters and the Mitchell Map (1755): settled colonies east of the Appalachians, Nova Scotia to Georgia
Georgia charter (1732-06-20) sets the start
layers.notes: Draw the colonies, not their sea-to-sea charter claims (those are the contested Ohio Country).

layers.name: Spanish Florida
sources: St. Augustine founded 1565-09-08
Treaty of Paris 1763 (Florida to Britain)
Popple, "A Map of the British Empire in America" (1733) for the Georgia-Florida frontier

layers.name: New Spain (northern frontier)
sources: Spanish missions and presidios of Texas, New Mexico and (from 1769) Alta California
Adams-Onis Treaty line (1819) for its northern edge late in the period
Treaty of Cordoba 1821-09-27 ends it
layers.notes: Northern borderlands only (Texas, New Mexico, the Californias). Its eastern edge with Louisiana was undefined until 1819: precision "contested" or "approximate". Mexico south of the frontier may be included.

layers.name: Rupert's Land (Hudson's Bay Company)
sources: Hudson's Bay Company charter (1670-05-02): the Hudson Bay drainage basin
Transfer to Canada 1870-07-15

layers.name: Province of Quebec
sources: Royal Proclamation of 1763, boundary clause
Kitchin, "A New Map of the Province of Quebec" (1763)
layers.notes: Seeded (candidate).

layers.name: British colonies (the thirteen, Nova Scotia)
sources: Mitchell Map (1755) for colony bounds
the Proclamation line for the western edge (geo.line.proclamation-1763)
layers.notes: East of the Proclamation line; the 1768 treaties (Fort Stanwix, Hard Labour) moved it west: one later state may follow.

layers.name: British East Florida
sources: Royal Proclamation of 1763 (bounds of East Florida)
Jefferys, "The Peninsula and Gulf of Florida" (1763)

layers.name: British West Florida
sources: Royal Proclamation of 1763: Gulf coast from the Apalachicola to the Mississippi, north to 31 degrees
1764 extension north to 32 deg 28 min
layers.notes: Draw the 1764 northern line if the source supports it.

layers.name: Indian Reserve (Proclamation of 1763)
sources: Royal Proclamation of 1763: lands west of the Proclamation line, east of the Mississippi, outside Quebec and the Floridas
layers.notes: British-claimed land reserved for Native nations: side "native".

layers.name: Spanish Louisiana
sources: Treaty of Fontainebleau (1762) and Treaty of Paris 1763: Louisiana west of the Mississippi, with New Orleans
Treaty of San Ildefonso 1800-10-01 ends it
layers.notes: Western edge undefined (Mississippi drainage); precision "approximate".

layers.name: Proclamation Line of 1763
sources: Royal Proclamation of 1763: the heads of rivers falling into the Atlantic
Treaties of Hard Labour and Fort Stanwix (1768) supersede it
layers.notes: Seeded (candidate): extend the northern end into New York before approving.

layers.name: Province of Quebec (Quebec Act)
sources: Quebec Act 1774: Quebec extended south to the Ohio and west to the Mississippi

layers.name: Indian Reserve (after the Quebec Act)
sources: Quebec Act 1774 (the reserve north of the Ohio becomes Quebec)
layers.notes: What is left south of the Ohio and west of the colonies.

layers.name: United States (Treaty of Paris)
sources: National Atlas of the United States, "Territorial Acquisitions of the United States" (USGS, public domain)
Treaty of Paris 1783, article 2 (boundaries)
layers.notes: Includes the western lands states claimed (later territories). The Florida border at 31 deg N was disputed with Spain until 1795.

layers.name: British North America
sources: Treaty of Paris 1783 (northern US border)
Treaty of 1818 (49th parallel to the Rockies)
Webster-Ashburton Treaty 1842 (Maine border)
layers.notes: Quebec (Upper and Lower Canada after 1791), Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Newfoundland; Rupert's Land is its own layer.

layers.name: Spanish Florida (East and West)
sources: Treaty of Paris 1783 (Floridas returned to Spain)
Pinckney's Treaty 1795 (31 deg N)
Adams-Onis Treaty, effective 1821-02-22
layers.notes: West Florida west of the Perdido was seized by the US in 1810-13: a later state may follow.

layers.name: French Louisiana
sources: Treaty of San Ildefonso 1800-10-01
Louisiana Purchase treaty 1803-04-30
layers.notes: Same ground as Spanish Louisiana (Spain still administered it).

layers.name: United States (Louisiana Purchase)
sources: National Atlas of the United States, "Territorial Acquisitions of the United States" (USGS, public domain)
layers.notes: The Purchase's northern and western edges follow the Mississippi-Missouri drainage until the 1818 and 1819 treaties.

layers.name: Russian America
sources: Russian-American Company charter 1799
Alaska transfer 1867-10-18

layers.name: Oregon Country (joint occupation)
sources: Treaty of 1818 (joint US-British occupation)
Adams-Onis (42 deg N south line) and the Russo-American Treaty of 1824 (54 deg 40 min north line)
layers.notes: Claimed by both: precision "contested".

layers.name: Missouri Compromise line (36 deg 30 min)
sources: Missouri Compromise 1820: 36 deg 30 min N across the Louisiana Purchase, west of Missouri
Kansas-Nebraska Act 1854-05-30 repeals it

layers.name: United States (Adams-Onis)
sources: National Atlas of the United States, "Territorial Acquisitions of the United States" (USGS, public domain)
Adams-Onis Treaty, effective 1821-02-22

layers.name: Mexico
sources: Treaty of Cordoba 1821-09-27
Adams-Onis line for the northern border
Natural Earth admin-0/admin-1 (public domain) where the border follows a modern one

layers.name: Republic of Texas
sources: Texas Declaration of Independence 1836-03-02
Texas claim to the Rio Grande (contested by Mexico)
layers.notes: Draw the claimed Rio Grande border; precision "contested".

layers.name: Mexico (after Texas)
sources: Natural Earth admin-0/admin-1 (public domain) where the border follows a modern one
the Nueces/Rio Grande dispute

layers.name: United States (Texas annexed)
sources: National Atlas of the United States, "Territorial Acquisitions of the United States" (USGS, public domain)

layers.name: United States (Oregon Treaty)
sources: National Atlas of the United States, "Territorial Acquisitions of the United States" (USGS, public domain)
Oregon Treaty 1846-06-15 (49th parallel)

layers.name: British North America (after Oregon)
sources: Oregon Treaty 1846
layers.notes: Adds the Pacific coast north of the 49th parallel.

layers.name: United States (Mexican Cession)
sources: National Atlas of the United States, "Territorial Acquisitions of the United States" (USGS, public domain)
Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo 1848-02-02

layers.name: Mexico (after the Mexican Cession)
sources: Natural Earth admin-0/admin-1 (public domain) where the border follows a modern one
Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo 1848

layers.name: United States (Gadsden Purchase)
sources: National Atlas of the United States, "Territorial Acquisitions of the United States" (USGS, public domain)
Gadsden Purchase 1853-12-30
layers.notes: Modern lower-48 outline: build it from Natural Earth.

layers.name: Mexico
sources: Natural Earth admin-0/admin-1 (public domain) where the border follows a modern one
layers.notes: The modern border: build it from Natural Earth admin-0.

layers.name: Confederate States
sources: the eleven seceded states (Tennessee seceded last, 1861-06-08)
Natural Earth admin-0/admin-1 (public domain) where the border follows a modern one: union of the eleven states' outlines
layers.notes: Never recognised: precision "contested" (it draws over the United States layer).

layers.name: British Columbia
sources: union of Vancouver Island and British Columbia 1866-11-19
joins Canada 1871-07-20

layers.name: Dominion of Canada
sources: British North America Act 1867: Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick
layers.notes: A later state (1870, Rupert's Land and Manitoba) is for a planning agent to add.

layers.name: United States (Alaska)
sources: National Atlas of the United States, "Territorial Acquisitions of the United States" (USGS, public domain)
Alaska transfer 1867-10-18
layers.notes: Overseas territories (1898) belong on a world view: a planning agent adds them.
